content.comment_body: Good morning, I need some assistance. I have a [product_name] program where a timer can be configured by the operator via the display. Is there a way to set minimum and maximum limits for this timer, which was created within the text message block on the screen?

It seems possible, but it requires some effort. You can't restrict the input directly, only check if the entered value falls within the allowed range after the fact. If it doesn't, you can prevent further action and show a message to the user.
I've attached a possible solution. Hope this helps.

Hello [user_name], Alternatively, you might use a muxer or arithmetic operation to route the timer value through a logic block. This can limit values, so if the input is too high or too low, it gets set to your predefined maximum or minimum. You should still display an error message if limits are exceeded. There is also a user-uploaded function block in the German section called 'Fenster-Verstärker' (UDF), which could be helpful. Greetings [user_name] (translated with Google)

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are exploring ways to set up limits for a configurable timer in a [product_name] program interface. Suggestions include validating values after input to ensure they fall within specified boundaries and using logic blocks to constrain timer values before they are applied. Error messaging for out-of-range entries is recommended, and reusable function blocks from other discussions may serve as practical solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to enforce minimum and maximum values for a configurable timer directly on the interface, either by restricting operator entry or by ensuring the timer always operates within limits.
